description: States jointly submit a dispute to the Court by compromis or special agreement.
notes: Strongest consent pathway because both parties agree to litigate the specific dispute.

description: A treaty clause gives the Court jurisdiction over disputes concerning interpretation or application of that treaty.
notes: Often central in modern ICJ litigation.

description: States accept compulsory jurisdiction under Article 36(2), often with reservations.
notes: Powerful but limited by reservations, reciprocity, and withdrawals.

description: A respondent state accepts jurisdiction after proceedings are initiated.
Authorized UN organs or agencies request an opinion on a legal question.
notes: Not a contentious case, but often doctrinally influential.

description: Interim orders preserving rights pending final decision when jurisdiction appears prima facie.
example: The Gambia v. Myanmar; South Africa v. Israel

description: Objections to jurisdiction or admissibility before merits.
UN Charter obligation to comply with ICJ judgments in cases to which a state is party.
notes: Security Council follow-up is politically constrained.
